title: Beef Nachos
subtitle: Spiced beef mince and melted cheese over tortilla chips
excerpt: Tortilla chips covered in spiced beef mince and generous cheddar, baked until the cheese bubbles, then topped with soured cream and jalapeños. A simpler version of loaded nachos that keeps the focus on the beef.
sourceNotes: Beef nachos: a simplified loaded nacho format focused on spiced beef mince and melted cheese. Developed from the Tex-Mex restaurant tradition that expanded the original 1943 nacho (tortilla chips, cheese, jalapeños) into a main-course sharing dish.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The beef can be cooked a day ahead and refrigerated. Assemble and bake just before serving.

content.text: Beef nachos strip the loaded nacho back to its essentials: crisp tortilla chips, spiced beef mince, and melted cheese, baked together and served with cold toppings on the side. The beef needs to be cooked until the pan is nearly dry before it goes on the chips; excess moisture makes the base layer soggy within minutes. Keep the beef filling lean and well-seasoned.

items.prepNote: bought tortilla chips, or corn tortillas cut into triangles and baked at 180°C for 10-12 minutes until crisp

content.text: Heat {{vegetable-oil}} of oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook {{onion}} of finely chopped onion for 5 minutes until soft. Add {{garlic}} of crushed garlic for 1 minute. Add {{beef-mince}} of beef mince and break up as it cooks. Once browned, add the chilli powder, cumin, and smoked paprika. Cook for 2-3 minutes more, stirring. The pan should look dry. Season with salt and set aside.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Spread the tortilla chips in an even layer across a large baking tray. Spoon the beef over the chips. Scatter the grated cheddar generously over the top.
Bake for 8-10 minutes until the cheese is fully melted and beginning to bubble at the edges. Serve straight from the tray with soured cream, jalapeños, and coriander.

items.symptom: Chips go soft before the cheese melts
items.cause: Beef filling too wet, or nachos left assembled too long before baking
items.fix: Cook the beef until the pan is completely dry. Assemble and put straight into the oven; don't leave them sitting.

items.symptom: Some chips burn while others are fine
items.cause: Uneven spread of chips or oven has hot spots
items.fix: Spread chips in a single even layer. Rotate the tray halfway through baking if your oven runs unevenly.

items.symptom: Cheese pools under the chips rather than over them
items.cause: Cheese scattered but not enough on top; slid underneath during baking
items.fix: Scatter the cheese across the very top after the beef. The cheese should sit on the surface and melt down, not underneath the beef.

items.cause: Mince steamed instead of frying, or spices not cooked off
items.fix: Break the mince up as it cooks so it's in small pieces that brown. Add the spices once the mince is browned and cook for 2-3 minutes to develop the flavour.

content.text: Beef nachos are the most common nacho order in US sports bars and casual restaurants: a large tray of chips, a substantial beef topping, melted cheese, and simple cold condiments. They sit between a bar snack and a meal, which is their practical value: enough for four to share as a starter, or two to eat as a main.
